note: The A shape of CAGED: open A moved up as a barre (its chord boxes pinned, so they stay the lesson's shapes), then the chord, arpeggio, major pentatonic and major scale in the same frets, the arpeggio alone, and the chord in the A shape and the E shape. The old Key selector is now moves (any key), so the text names the key only as {{=key}} and a {{?key}} line says what stays the same; each block has one feel or one thing to notice.

exercise.title: CAGED: the A shape
exercise.why: A barre chord with its root on the A string is the open A chord moved up the neck, so a chord you know in the E shape has a second place, with its own arpeggio, pentatonic and scale around it.

cells.text:
Press the chord box below to hear A. Then press the three chord boxes under it: each is the same shape moved up the neck, with finger 1 in place of the nut.
Play all four, and say each chord's name as you land on it: the name is the note under finger 1 on the A string.

Press Play on each of the four panels below to hear it: the {{=key}} chord in the A shape, its arpeggio, the {{=key}} major pentatonic scale and the {{=key}} major scale, all in the same frets.
Play each one on your guitar, starting and ending on a root.
Practice until you can see the chord inside the scale.
{{?key}}In another key the shape moves along the neck, and every note keeps its place inside it.

Press Play below to hear the {{=key}} arpeggio run up and back down. Then play it yourself, from the lowest ringed {{1}} to the highest note and back.
Practice until your fingers find the next note without you looking.

Press Play on the two chord panels below to hear {{=key}} in the A shape, then higher up in the E shape. Play one, then the other, on your guitar.
When you change the shape, the chord keeps its name and its notes, and only their places on the neck are new.
